numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Probit log-likelihood is computed as log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1)), so each observation with q*XB below about -8 contributes the constant log(eps) = -36.04 instead of log(Phi(z)); for the reproducer model.loglike(params) returns -155.934 versus exact -1924.904. Score uses the same clipped cdf in pdf/cdf, so score of extreme observations is ~0 (reproducer gives [-4.874, 7.393] vs exact [-64.891, -2393.273]); hessian returns nan below z = -38 (np.isnan(model.hessian(params)).any() is True). fit(method="bfgs") stops at [-0.036, 1.72] with bse [nan nan] and llf -155.067.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: loglike should equal stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum() (-1924.904 for the reproducer); score should be [-64.891, -2393.273]; hessian should be finite; bfgs should converge to the exact optimum [-0.129, 0.077] with llf -202.674 and finite bse.
trigger_conditions: one extreme, misclassified observation in the sample (e.g. x value 40.0 with y=0)
q * XB below about -8 (loglike clipped flat at log(eps))
q * XB below about -38 causes hessian nan from 0/0
fit(method="bfgs") on such data converges to spurious optimum with nan bse

input_output_examples.input: params = np.array([0.0, 1.5]) with reproducer data (n=300, one extra observation x=40.0, y=0)

oracle_clues: reference values from scipy.stats.norm.logcdf / scipy.special log_ndtr and norm.logpdf
PR #10229 regression tests compare against scipy log_ndtr/norm.logcdf and finite-difference / complex-step derivative checks
newton and bfgs should converge to the same optimum as scipy.optimize.minimize of exact log-likelihood

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Linear predictor q*XB below about -8 (clipped cdf flat at log(eps)), below about -38 (log(cdf) underflows to -inf, Hessian nan), and extreme values z in [-1e4, 1e4] in the test
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=1e-14 for the analogous Logit test; no tolerance stated for the Probit test beyond assert_allclose against scipy.stats.norm.logcdf
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: Probit loglike at params [0.0, 1.5] gives -155.934 versus exact -1924.904 (stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum()) with one extreme misclassified observation x=40.0 and y=0
Score at same params gives [-4.874, 7.393] versus exact [-64.891, -2393.273], a wrong-signed score
BFGS fit returns params [-0.036, 1.72] with bse [nan, nan] and llf -155.067, while exact optimum is [-0.129, 0.077] with llf -202.674
Clipped cdf log(clip(cdf(z), eps, 1)) is flat at log(eps) for z below about -8; log(cdf(z)) underflows to -inf below about -38
Formula violated: log-likelihood should equal sum of log(Phi(z)) with z = q*XB, computed via scipy log_ndtr / norm.logcdf; score uses Mills ratio exp(logpdf - log_ndtr) instead of pdf/clipped cdf
Test test_probit_loglikeobs_extreme_linpred uses linspace(-1e4, 1e4, 50) and asserts finiteness of loglikeobs, score_obs, hessian and agreement with stats.norm.logcdf
Commit states the fix is the Probit counterpart of the Logit overflow fix in gh-3923
reproduction_risks: Reproducer's printed exact-value comparisons (-1924.904, exact optimum values) are from issue text and depend on numpy default_rng(1) draws; the issue reproducer code is truncated in one passage
Hessian and score rely on warnings being turned into errors in the test; the fix replaces the clipping in the score/hessian paths only as described in the commit
Versions of scipy/numpy are not stated in the passages
